item.title: 'Point of no return' if Israel-Hamas truce fails: US envoy to Gaza board
item.description:
The high representative for Gaza in US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace warned Wednesday of a "point of no return" if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire breaks down.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, facing a tough re-election fight, earlier this month publicly rejected the latest part of a US plan aimed at ending the devastating Gaza war.

item.title: US targets Palestine Action in counterterrorism effort against 'far-left' groups
item.description:
By Daphne Psaledakis

WASHINGTON, Aug 26 (Reuters) - The United States designated Palestine Action on Wednesday as a terrorist group, as President Donald Trump's administration seeks to crack down on left-wing groupsin its counterterrorism efforts.

item.title: Kremlin says US spy chief met with Russian counterparts during Moscow visit
item.description:
MOSCOW/WASHINGTON, Aug 26 (Reuters) - U.S. CIA Director John Ratcliffe spoke with Russian intelligence officials during a visit to Moscow but did not meet President Vladimir Putin, the Kremlin said on Wednesday of a trip that U.S. President Donald Trump described as "semi-routine."

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters Putin had been briefed on the outcome of Tuesday's visit, which came as the war in Ukraine drags on and as efforts to reach a lasting peace between the United States and Iran have stalled.

item.title: Iran and Oman reach agreements on share of Hormuz and revenues, Revolutionary Guards say
item.description:
Aug 26 (Reuters) - Iran and Oman have reached agreements on their share of the Strait of Hormuz and its revenues, Iran's Revolutionary Guards spokesperson said, according to a report by the semi-official Tasnim news agency on Wednesday.

The spokesperson said the U.S. was obstructing negotiations between Oman and Iran, leading to them being delayed

(Reporting by Menna Alaa El-Din and Elwely Elwelly; Editing by Andrew Heavens)

item.title: Turkey says SDF dissolution will help with Syrian unity
item.description:
ISTANBUL, Aug 26 (Reuters) - Turkey's ruling AK Party welcomes the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces as an important step towards strengthening Syrian unity, a spokesman for President Tayyip Erdogan's party said on Wednesday.

NATO member Turkey has emerged as one of the main allies of neighbouring Syria's President Ahmed al-Sharaa after he toppled Bashar al-Assad's decades-long rule.

item.title: Saudi diversification drive on display in France as US reach shows limits
item.description:
Saudi investment in France reflects the fast-growing rapprochement between Paris and Riyadh as power dynamics are reshaped across the Middle East, with the kingdom seeking to diversify its partnerships without jeopardising its strategic alliance with the United States. 

The visit to Paris by Saudi Arabia's de facto ruler, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, provided the occasion on Monday to announce 21 agreements and memorandums of understanding between the two countries.

item.title: Gaza's children lose simple joy as Israel warns against kite-flying
item.description:
There are few joys left for 10-year-old Ahmed Hamdouna, whose childhood has already been scarred by years of war and displacement in Gaza. 

Now, what little reprieve he found playing with scraps of plastic and sticks has also been torn away, as Israel warns it will step up military operations in the territory if kites continue to land on the Israeli side of the border.

"My father stopped me from flying my kites because of the occupation's threats," said Ahmed, who has been displaced to Deir el-Balah in the central Gaza Strip.

item.title: US Senate Democrats urge Israel to rein in West Bank violence
item.description:
(Corrects number of Democrats signing letter to 45, not 42)

By Richard Cowan

WASHINGTON, Aug 26 (Reuters) - U.S. Senate Democrats on Wednesday urged Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to rein in a "surge" of violence by West Bank settlers and mass arrests of Palestinians by Israeli security forcesin the occupied territory.

Inthe letter to Netanyahu, seen by Reuters and signed by 45 of the Senate's 47-member Democratic caucus, the lawmakers noted increasing levels of "fatal violence by settlers."
